plain: Michels raises the idea that Edward Condon, a scientist who publicly dismissed UFOs, may have been blackmailed into doing so. He says, without naming a source, that while Condon was being investigated in the 1950s for communist sympathies, an agent of the FBI, the US federal police agency, named Guy Hottel was quietly building a file of field reports on him in the background. If true, it would mean the scientific case against UFOs was shaped by pressure from the government.
